address: Silver Birches, 234 Melton Road, Hickling Pastures LE14 3QG (Monday text6 reads 'LE143QG3' — likely typo, verify)
lead_profile_text: Looking to move abroad and short let my home
property_situation: Family home, currently lived in and fully furnished. Owners (Byron and wife) relocating UK to US and want to keep it as a UK base: personal use June-September every year, let the other 8 months. Long let ruled out because of the personal-use requirement. Mortgage £1,400/month per Monday (lead said they need to 'clear about $25,000' a year). Wife currently deciding what furniture to take to the US. Move date not stated.
property_type: 3-bed detached family home, rural village (Vale of Belvoir, Leicestershire/Notts border); owners say they have 'done a lot to the house'
primary_blocker: Actively comparing several providers (Stayful was the second of 'a few more folks lined up') on fees, with a joint decision with his wife and an unconfirmed relocation date; explicitly 'not going to make a decision really quick'

delay_signals.context: Opening statement of his goal; the property is currently their lived-in home and the wife is still choosing what furniture to take to the States

meeting_flow.opening_phrase: So what I'll do is I'll go through the figures. Then I'll go through our services, sort of how it will tie into what you're ultimately trying to achieve, which is ... a base in the UK whilst you're living abroad, but also having income so it covers the mortgage and all the other costs.
rapport_topics: Zac being based in Leicestershire — 'you are local then, we're just up the street'
Areas Stayful manages in the Midlands and nationally
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: So this is what we've managed to project from your property.
meeting_flow.income_intro: So we're looking at about £77,000 of gross revenue a year. About £6,500 per month. That breaks down into £40,000 per year of net revenue and £3,300 of profit.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: So really what we do is we focus on listing on 3 different platforms, which is Airbnb, Booking.com, and our own direct booking site.
meeting_flow.pre_close_setup: What I'll put is a bit like an action plan together. So it'll have everything you're going to need to know ... our management agreement in there as well, the figures we've shown
meeting_flow.meeting_2_ask: If you've got any sort of photos you can send over to us ... I'll drop you a WhatsApp after this.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: We're looking at your fees and monthly charges and stuff, and it seems a little bit more than what we found elsewhere
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Went straight into the figures and then explained gross-to-net: platform commission 15%, cleaning/laundry ~18% (guest-paid, backed out of gross), management 15%.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: I had, I forget, 30 to 40% ... that's scary as hell ... So I'm glad you're breaking it down for me.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Are we talking about a full 12-month rental there, or is that for the 8 months? ... the time that we'd like it for is the summer, which I'm sure is probably the height of demand
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Based on 12 months; best month July ~£5,000; worst ~£2,000; with June-September removed, roughly £2,000-£4,000 net per let month — admitted he'd need to come back on the 8-month average.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: I figured as much that we'd probably work it out.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I had a figure of £42 a month ... is that the platform fee or is that different?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: That's a software charge — part of our management fee.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: The cleaning fee and laundry ... 18%. So the client is responsible for that, and it's passed on to me as the owner, or how?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Showed the owner calendar and a sample monthly PDF statement — guest pays nightly rate plus cleaning fee; the cleaning fee goes to the cleaner, owner is paid out the nightly-rate portion.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: How you got so wise to being able to apply these numbers to where we live
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Stayful's software averages 12 nearby competitor properties; expect 10-20% less until reviews build, which is why year-one focus is reviews.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: We've done a lot to the house ... obviously it needs to be evaluated. So how would that process be?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Next steps if going ahead: key safes, onboarding form, inspection and deep clean, linens, photographer, then live — about 2-3 weeks.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Might we be able to see some of the — what you sent, the numbers you quoted, the spreadsheets, or is that proprietary?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: I'll put an action plan together with everything covered, the figures and our management agreement.

conversion_gaps.gap: Fee credibility is the swing factor against competitors, yet the fee was quoted as 15% (not 15% + VAT) and the £42/mo software fee was described as 'part of our management fee' when it is a separate deduction
conversion_gaps.evidence: "it seems a little bit more than what we found elsewhere" / "That's part of our management fee, that is."
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: State 15% + VAT and the £42/mo software fee as separate lines on every call; disclose corrections in writing immediately (done in the action plan/email)

conversion_gaps.gap: Figures were presented for 12 months although the lead only wants 8 let months; Zac could not give the 8-month average live
conversion_gaps.evidence: "It's hard for me to say what the average is with how much performance taken out. I might have to come back to you a bit on that."
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: When the pre-call brief or opening reveals seasonal personal use, re-cut the forecast for the let months only (8-month net ~£26k) before quoting annual totals

conversion_gaps.gap: No follow-up call booked and no decision date — lead is comparing several providers
conversion_gaps.evidence: "we've got a few more folks that are lined up, so we're going to look at all options and we will let you know"
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Before ending, ask when they expect to have spoken to everyone and book a follow-up for just after that date (Calendly link offered only in writing)

conversion_gaps.gap: Relocation date, mortgage lender consent for letting, and holiday-let insurance / non-resident landlord tax not raised on the call
conversion_gaps.evidence: Move date never asked; deck showed 'No mortgage' although Monday records a £1,400/month mortgage
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: For ABROAD leads, ask the departure date and mortgage status in the first five minutes; cover lender consent, insurance and NRL scheme in the written follow-up

conversion_gaps.gap: Deck included an implausible demand driver (Nottingham City Airport / Tollerton airfield 'flight crew layovers') for a rural village
conversion_gaps.evidence: Drive intelligence entry: removed from the action plan and disclosed
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Sanity-check auto-generated demand drivers before rural meetings

zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Let the fee-comparison objection sit while walking through the cost stack, then used concrete software demos (calendar, statement) to answer mechanics questions; defers precise re-cuts to the written action plan rather than guessing

what_they_focused_on: What the 12-month figures mean for an 8-month let
How cleaning and the £42 fee flow through
How the numbers were derived for his specific area
Whether the upgrades to the house are reflected
what_they_needed_most: Covering ~£16,800/yr mortgage from the 8 let months
Keeping the home available every summer
Fee transparency he can compare like-for-like
Time to compare providers with his wife
what_fell_flat: Annual (12-month) figures when he only wants to let 8 months
Fee statement that omitted VAT and misdescribed the software fee
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For ABROAD leads with seasonal personal use, cut the forecast to the let months before the call, lead with the remote-owner mechanics and a complete, VAT-inclusive fee stack, and book a follow-up tied to the end of their provider comparison
